question: Descriptive repeat of tool adoption with the corrected find_affected_files description on the same 40 historical scenarios.
runtime: Clean product build 3d91bb84, archived scenario trees and graph bytes, same Sonnet model ID as the September registration. Time and changes elsewhere on the offered surface may affect adoption. No causal language.

sample.reuse: Existing archive and scenario rows kept byte-for-byte in their original location. The new file carries the new runner registration ID and the same scenario rows; this is intentional reuse rather than a new independent sample. No comparison of the grep or prefilled arms is attempted because neither offers the corrected wording.

unit_and_truth.unit: one historical change to one file, at most one scenario per file
unit_and_truth.ground_truth: a file is affected when it carries a type error after applying exactly that file's diff that it did not carry before; errors compared as (file, TS code, message) multisets with line and column ignored; adjudicated by hand before any arm runs, removals only with a written reason
unit_and_truth.$comment: The truth definition is not touched. Changing the ruler and the tool in the same step would leave nothing comparable.

run_conditions.per_scenario_base: the commit's parent SHA, recorded in the scenario file with the graph's sha256
run_conditions.$comment_ceiling: The maintainer raised the ceiling from USD 20 to USD 40 on 2026-09-18, before the run.
run_conditions.cost_estimate: From the v4 pilot on bastra-recall (6 arms, $0.9919, mean $0.1653 per arm, mean 157 168 input tokens per arm): 3 arms x $0.1653 = $0.496 per scenario, so 40 scenarios = $19.84 and 45 = $22.32. Both sit under the $40 ceiling, which leaves room for the larger prompts a pooled sample may carry. The runner stops BEFORE the arm that would cross the ceiling, not after.
run_conditions.$comment_cost: Enforced by the runner, not documented at it: every arm's cost is summed and the next arm only starts while the ceiling is still out of reach at the mean cost of the arms that finished. Raising it is a decision, not a flag someone reaches for at 2 a.m. (CODE_ROI_COST_CEILING).

finalisation_and_ceiling.$comment: AMENDED 2026-09-19, before the first arm of the main run. NO THRESHOLD, ARM, SAMPLE OR VERDICT CHANGES — this sharpens two rules the runner was already meant to follow, both found by a counter-review of the runner rather than by a result. (1) FINALISATION. An arm was finalised on exit 0 plus the presence of a `result` event. The installed CLI (2.1.278) also emits a `result` when it gives up — `subtype` is one of success / error_during_execution / error_max_turns / error_max_budget_usd / error_max_structured_output_retries — and a `--max-budget-usd` stop exits 0, so a truncated arm could be finalised and its partial `FILES:` line scored as an answer. An arm now counts as finished only on exit 0 AND `is_error === false` AND `subtype === "success"`; everything else is re-run by the next helping. All 107 archived result events across code-roi-v2, both pilots and the adoption run are `success` / `is_error:false`, so no existing transcript changes status. (2) THE CEILING RECKONING. Finished cost and total burden are now kept apart: the ceiling is checked against the burden (finished arms plus what aborts were charged), while the per-arm projection is the mean of the FINISHED arms only, so a run of failures cannot inflate its own reading. An abort is charged its own `result` event where it has one, otherwise that mean, otherwise the per-arm figure in `cost_estimate` above ($0.1653) — previously it was charged $0 before the first finished arm, so a sample whose every arm aborted would have walked the whole list without the ceiling binding. Abort costs are written to `<arm>.failed-<stamp>.meta.json` when they happen and read back on resume, together with the finished arms, so a resumed helping starts from the real spend. Implementation: `packages/eval/code-roi/v2/arm-cost.mjs`, split out of `run-arms-v3.mjs`.

stretched_run.$comment: AMENDED 2026-09-19, before the first arm of the main run: the run is taken in helpings across several subscription-quota windows (`run-arms-v3.mjs --max-scenarios N`). Cause is the quota, nothing about the measurement. Sample, scenario order, arm order, thresholds and both verdicts are unchanged; a scenario that is started is normally finished across all three arms within the same helping. An abort or the cost ceiling can still cut a scenario short mid-arm — that is exactly what `finalisation_and_ceiling` above exists to catch — and when it does, the arm it interrupted is simply not counted as run and the next helping runs it, so a pair can be torn ACROSS helpings but is never silently completed with a partial answer. A report from a partially finished archive is labelled `incomplete (x/40)`: the effect is computed on complete triples only, adoption on every scenario whose B arm has run, and neither reaches a verdict below min_scenarios.

build_pin.$comment: AMENDED 2026-09-19, before the first arm of the main run, by a Codex counter-review (numbered 4 in this file's own review history) — found on a dry read of the runner, not from a result. NO THRESHOLD, ARM, SAMPLE OR VERDICT CHANGES; this closes a gap in HOW the runner is started, not in what it measures. `run-arms-v3.mjs` imports `packages/daemon/dist` directly, never `src`, and the start command documented until now (`CODE_ROI_OUT=… node run-arms-v3.mjs --max-scenarios 8`) neither built it nor checked it. Codex found `packages/daemon/dist/.build-revision` reading a commit several revisions behind HEAD at the moment this registration's own thresholds were being finalised — an unguarded first arm that morning would have measured a server nobody had reviewed at HEAD and called it this registration. The `stretched_run` amendment above makes it worse than a one-off: a run taken in helpings across days means a REBUILD between two helpings could serve two different product revisions under one archive and one report, with nothing to say so.
build_pin.preflight: Before touching an arm, every invocation of `run-arms-v3.mjs` now checks, in order: (1) `packages/daemon/dist/.build-revision` exists, names `git rev-parse HEAD` exactly, AND says `dirty=false`; a build stamped dirty can contain uncommitted source while still naming the same HEAD, so revision equality alone is not provenance; (2) the current worktree is clean over `packages/daemon/src` and `packages/eval` (`git status --porcelain`); (3) the four `arms.frozen_surface` hashes above, recomputed from the BUILT `dist` artefacts with the identical computation `code-graph-affected.test.ts` pins from `src`, still match this registration. Any failure aborts before an arm starts and names which check failed and why. The dirty-stamp rejection was added by counter-review 5 before the first arm; the sample, arms, thresholds and verdicts are unchanged. `--preflight-only` runs these checks and exits without starting an arm — the dry-run this amendment was verified with.
build_pin.pin: What passes the preflight is written to `build-pin.json` in the archive (`CODE_ROI_OUT`) on the FIRST helping: the HEAD sha, the dist revision stamp, the four frozen-surface hashes, and a sha256 of every dist artefact the arms are actually served from (`code-graph/*.js`, `tool-defs.js`, `mcp-instructions.js`). Every LATER helping of the same archive is checked against this pin, field by field; a mismatch aborts with every differing field named (never just the first) and never re-pins or overwrites — the same discipline `mutation_gate.population_pinned` already uses for the synthetic gate's own population. Every arm's meta (finished or aborted) carries the pin's signature beside it, and `evaluate-v4.mjs` reads it back to report `mixed_builds` in the report — true if any transcript in the archive was not served by the archive's pinned build.
build_pin.start_command: npm run build && CODE_ROI_OUT=<historical-arm-b-archive> node packages/eval/code-roi/v2/run-arms-v3.mjs --max-scenarios 8 — the `npm run build &&` is new; the rest is unchanged from the command recorded before this amendment.
build_pin.implementation: packages/eval/code-roi/v2/build-pin.mjs, called from `run-arms-v3.mjs`'s `main()` before `scenarios.json` is even read, and from `evaluate-v4.mjs` when the report is built.

run_conditions.frozen_archive: The historical v2 archive is never written by a v4 script — `archive.mjs` refuses it, because the v3 report is only reproducible while that archive is untouched.

reporting: Completed and aborted arms separately; adoption for each tool, per-scenario pairing to prior B, precision and input tokens descriptive only, cost; keep partial toll separate.
limitations: Archives and gold truth stay read-only. No vault, raw personal document, or private gold case is provided to the model. Claude runs from the scenario-only sandbox with no Bash or model spawning.

result.historical_artifact: Historical Arm B archive from the code-awareness-change-impact registration
result.adoption_interpretation: Descriptive repeat of registered Arm B, no arm A or prefilled rerun. Same advertised model ID; CLI and build differ. This does not isolate the effect of the wording.
